nodes.label: A 49-year-old woman presented with healed ulcers of the lower lip and nasal dorsum and a nonhealing ulcer of the left lateral infraorbital area
Patient reported several years of facial ulcers described as 'scratches' developing over weeks to months into red, indurated, tender ulcers that finally crusted and healed
Review of systems was positive for dry mouth, Raynaud phenomenon, morning joint pain, mild hand and ankle swelling, and dysphagia
Physical examination revealed healed ulcers on lower lip and nasal dorsum and a nonhealing ulcer in left lateral infraorbital area

Later ocular findings included diplopia, sense of fullness below left eye, restriction of left eye into hypotropic and exotropic position, full-thickness defect through lateral lower eyelid, exposed conjunctiva and bony orbital rim
Serologic testing is positive for ANA (1:360) with decreased complement C4
Serum angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) level is elevated
Orbital biopsy reveals foreign-body granulomas containing polarizable material
Foreign-body granulomatous reaction (e.g., to injected filler material)
Specific autoimmune serologies (anti-dsDNA, anti-Ro/SSA, anti-La/SSB, anti-Sm, anti-RNP) have not been performed
Chest CT for hilar lymphadenopathy has not been performed
No documented history of trauma or foreign-body/filler exposure
Direct immunofluorescence, salivary biopsy, and serum calcium testing data are missing
Rheumatoid factor (RF) has not been performed
Schirmer test and salivary flow measurement have not been performed
